Goal
* Please mention that "digisible" is a French word, to avoid confusion for players who may assume it's a typo.

* Please remove the word "evenly".

* The statement should explicitly explain that {{ZERO}} and {{DIVISIBLE}} cannot be reported simultaneously. If a number contains the digit {{0}}, divisibility by its digits is not evaluated for that digit because division by zero is undefined.

* It's unclear what should be output if [[N]] itself is digisible. If [[N]] is guaranteed not to be digisible, please state this explicitly in the Constraints section. Otherwise, please specify the expected output in that case.

Output
* Please add "<<Line 1>>:" and "<<Line 2>>:" before the corresponding output descriptions.

* Please format "ZERO", "DUPLICATE", "DIVISIBLE" and "+" as {{constants}}.

* Please specify the order in which multiple failure reasons should be output.

* The phrase "next digisible number greater than or equal to N" is contradictory in itself, since "next" normally implies a strictly greater value. Please reword this for clarity.

Constraints
* The variable name "num" is inconsistent with the rest of the statement. Please change it to [[N]].

* Please change the upper bound of [[N]] from 999999 to 99999 as [[N]] never exceeds 99999 in the existing cases. Please also specify its lower bound, i.e. 1.

Stub generator
* Line 1: Please change "string(9000000)" to "int".

Cases
* Test 2 is incorrect: for input 15, the expected output is listed as ZERO 18264.

* Both Test 2 and Test 4 use 15 as input. Please remove one of them.

* Please group the cases so that each test and its corresponding validator cover the same scenario. Create additional cases where necessary to form matching pairs. For example:

  • Test 1 and Validator 1: DIVISIBLE

  • Test 2 and Validator 2: ZERO

  • Test 3 and Validator 3: DUPLICATE

  • Test 4 and Validator 4: ZERO+DUPLICATE

  (etc.)

Thanks.

❌ Rejected the contribution.
Comment: I agree with @5DN1L. Please change your clash to WIP (work in progress) for the meantime, as I think the concept is nice, but the output just needs to be worked on. Thanks!

❌ Rejected the contribution.
Comment: This clash in essence suffers from a binary output issue (i.e. only 2 possible output variations of true and false). The output requiring to repeat the input number does not help resolve the issue.
I hope you received enough feedback from the community to improve your contribution. Once you have made the necessary updates, publish your contribution!

I like the puzzle!
But pay attention to correctly use of the terms "number" and "digit" in the description.
It should say:

A number is said to be "digisible" if it satisfies the following conditions:
(1) None of its digits are zero
(2) It is written with all different digits
(3) it is divisible by each of its digits

Test carried out with regex methods easily provided you know how to use them. In the output I think it is useless to have to specify the number as input.
Fun: 4/5
Difficulty: 2/5
Statement: 5 / 5
Relevance of test games: 3 / 5
Maybe add the requirement that the failed requirement (aka the reason for failure) must be added to the output and the digits that caused it?

Looks like "digisible" is a French word. Not sure what the English equivalent is...

This clash in essence suffers from a binary output issue (i.e. only 2 possible output variations of true and false). The output requiring to repeat the input number does not help resolve the issue. Please fix it.

Thanks.

In what ways?

(1) Check if there are any zeroes
(2) Check if there are duplicate digits
(3) Check if the number is divisible by all of its digits - maximum of 9

The puzzle itself is not that difficult.
Suggestion : printing the digit at which one test fails if it does fail and if it is true then the last digit checked
He is just making fun of me! I know him, he is a friend of mine
Ah, I see - sorry for the confusion then :)
